articles.title: Edmonton-based video game studio BioWare shutting down after more than 30 years
articles.summary: Video game publisher Electronic Arts is shutting down the popular Edmonton-based game development studio BioWare, known for the games Baldur's Gate and Dragon Age, after more than three decades.

image.caption: Video game publisher Electronic Arts announced Wednesday that it is shutting down Edmonton-based BioWare, a popular video game studio, after more than three decades. (Jae C. Hong/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Canada·New
Video game publisher Electronic Arts is shutting down the popular Edmonton-based game development studio BioWare, known for the games Baldur's Gate and Dragon Age, after more than three decades.
Influential game development company known for Baldur's Gate and Dragon Age
Video game publisher Electronic Arts is shutting down the popular Edmonton-based game development studio BioWare after more than three decades.
BioWare announced the closure on social media Wednesday following a report by Bloomberg that also said the company is laying off 400 people, including about 50 at BioWare.
It also confirmed the upcoming Mass Effect game, the fifth in a series since 2007, has been cancelled.
BioWare was founded in 1995 and acquired by Electronic Arts (EA) in 2007.
"It's a pretty sad day," BioWare co-founder Trent Oster told CBC Radio. "I mean, 30 plus years ago we built something I think was pretty awesome. And it's pretty sad to see the end of the dream."

The Redwood Shores, California-based maker of popular titles like Battlefield and The Sims closed the $55 billion US sale of its business to Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund PIF, investment firm Silver Lake Partners and Affinity Partners, which is run by U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner.

items: After a pandemic boom, Canada's video game industry is taking a hit
Union wants federal scrutiny of $55B US Electronic Arts sale over national security risks
Electronic Arts acquisition by private equity sparks more uncertainty for Canadian gaming industry

blocks.text: Representatives for EA did not immediately respond to a message seeking comment on the layoffs.

"What generations of BioWare built together is something to celebrate and remember," the studio said via social media. "These games became so much more because you played them, debated your choices, fell in love with characters, and made these worlds your own."

BioWare built its reputation on immersive role-playing adventures, from sword-and-sorcery fantasies like Baldur's Gate and Dragon Age to science fiction epics like Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic and Mass Effect.
Oster, who is now the CEO of gaming company Beamdog, said back in its early days, BioWare was a magical place to be.

"We went from a bunch of clueless kids trying to make a game just for the hell of it to literally being the best in the world at what we did," he said. "During the time I was there, it went from six people to 420, and it was just a massive growth. Honestly, it was an amazing experience."

But the company's later effort to branch out into multiplayer shooters, 2019's Anthem, steered away from the studio's strength as a creator of compelling single-player narratives. It failed to find the sort of loyal audience that keeps online hits like Fortnite and Overwatch popular.

items: How three Edmonton doctors turned their medical software company BioWare into a gaming powerhouse
Edmonton-based indie game studio latest to take blockbuster-making skills and get 'pretty risky'

blocks.text: Meanwhile the latest installments of BioWare's two most popular original franchises — 2017's Mass Effect: Andromeda and 2024's Dragon Age: The Veilguard — met with mixed reviews and disappointed many fans.
A new chapter of Mass Effect was in development before BioWare announced its shutdown.

articles.title: Man fined after 700 frozen and taxidermied animals found on Victorian property
articles.summary:
Antiques store owner, 74, pleads guilty to 13 charges after regulator uncovers hundreds of animals at his home and shop

The white-walled room packed with magpies, galahs and sulphur-crested…

blocks.text: The white-walled room packed with magpies, galahs and sulphur-crested cockatoos, foxes and possums is eerily quiet. As a video pans across shelves filled with these and many other species, there is no flapping or squawking or hissing; the animals are frozen and silent.
They are among the more than 700 native animals that were found illegally taxidermied and frozen that were seized from the property of a Victorian antiques store owner last year.

On Tuesday, 74-year-old Glenn Richard Rollo was fined $10,000 by a court after he pleaded guilty to 13 charges, including including selling and possessing protected and threatened wildlife and failing to provide treatment to a sick animal.

The regulator searched his property as part of a broader crackdown on the illegal wildlife trade, executing search warrants for the man’s store and home in April last year. Restrictions on selling and possessing threatened and protected species apply to both living and dead animals.

During their search they found 14 freezers containing animals. Across the property they found hundreds of dead reptiles, native birds and mammals, including 78 emus, 42 brushtail possums and 26 echidnas. They also found the remains of threatened species, including the barking owl, diamond python and Murray River short-necked turtle.

In addition to the dead animals, 15 live reptiles were found in enclosures, including North American red-eared slider turtles and corn snakes. Six of the reptiles, the regulator said, were not being kept under the required animal welfare standards.
The regulator said the man did not have the licence of authorisation under Victoria’s wildlife laws to obtain or possess the animals.

Wildlife in Victoria is protected under the Wildlife Act 1975, which outlaws taking native animals without approval. A commercial wildlife licence or private wildlife licence is required to trade dead animals.
Victorians who wish to taxidermy animals are also required obtain a licence under the conservation regulator.

During an appearance before Kynton local court on Tuesday, magistrate Patrick Southey reportedly told the man: “It is bewildering that a man of your intelligence and knowledge and love of wildlife would arrogantly flout the law so comprehensively.”

The conservation regulator director of regulatory operations, Cal Heppell, said: “The scale of offending in this case highlights why Victoria has strong protections in place for wildlife and animal welfare.
“Our laws and permit systems help protect wildlife from unlawful exploitation, ensure animals are appropriately cared for and safeguard Victoria’s environment and biodiversity from potential threats.
“These requirements are not optional. Anyone who keeps, trades or possesses wildlife must comply with the law.”
Victoria Animal Justice party MP Georgie Purcell said the wildlife laws in Victoria are not strong enough and called on the government to modernise the 50-year-old welfare act.
“This is a horrific case that has rattled our community of Kyneton but it should serve as a wake-up call as to just how broken our so-called wildlife protection laws are here in Victoria,” she said.

Purcell said that the $10,000 fine for possessing 700 dead native animals and keeping reptiles in poor conditions was “barely a deterrent and doesn’t send a message to the community that wildlife are respected and protected in Victoria”.

“The government talks a big game about protecting wildlife but cases like this show just how badly our native animals are being let down. If hundreds of native animals can end up dead in someone’s collection, questions need to be asked why the government has continued to stall when it comes to ensuring these laws meet community expectations.”

articles.title: Man arrested for allegedly making threats at Hannah Beazley’s electorate office while armed with nunchucks
articles.summary:
Perth man charged with ‘being armed in a way that may cause fear’ days after Helen Haines allegedly attacked with 4WD outside her Victorian office

  • Get our

blocks.text: A man has been charged after allegedly threatening staff and wielding nunchucks at the electoral office of the Western Australian local government minister, Hannah Beazley.

The arrest on Thursday came after federal independent MP Helen Haines was hospitalised with severe injuries after an alleged attack outside her electorate office in Wangaratta in Victoria earlier in the week.
Electoral staff at Beazley’s Victoria Park office in Perth called police after a man caused a disturbance on Wednesday afternoon.
Police said they received reports the man was making verbal threats while in possession of an “improvised martial arts weapon” described as “nunchucks”.

They arrested the 56-year-old man nearby and took him into custody. On Thursday he was charged with being armed in a way that may cause fear, making unlawful threats and cannabis possession. Nobody was injured in the incident.
The man was refused bail to appear at Perth magistrates court on Thursday.
Beazley was not in the office at the time but told reporters on Wednesday evening her staff were “rattled” by the “confronting situation”.
“He was [allegedly] being very threatening. He did want access to me, I believe, but we don’t know his motivations at all,” the minister said.
Beazley said there had been two staff members in the office at the time. The man allegedly attempted to lean through the security screen but her staff were a safe distance away, she said.
“It’s not the first time I’ve had threats made against me.
“My primary concern is the welfare of my staff, obviously. That was very rattling for them. They called the police.”
The prime minister, Anthony Albanese, said Hannah Beazley was a friend “because I’m a good friend of her dad”, the former Labor defence minister Kim Beazley.
“This is far too prevalent,” Albanese told Perth radio on Thursday. “It’s not who we are as Australians. We can have our discussions and debates and settle those issues at the ballot box.”
‘A unique and pernicious form of attack’
The governor general, Sam Mostyn, speaking generally on Thursday, discussed the gendered dynamics of threats and abuse directed at women in high-profile positions.
“Like any woman who has stepped up into any position across any part of our society, there is a unique and pernicious form of attack that comes our way,” Mostyn told ABC TV.

“I still receive that online. In fact, I was just saddened this morning to see some of the comments on my own Instagram page, in capitals with expletives, once again questioning the very nature of what it is that I do.
“Women across the country know that there are certain things that are reserved for women … that go to our gender and they are often vicious and just despicable.”

blocks.caption: Former independent MP Cathy McGowan at a community vigil for Helen Haines. Photograph: Mridula Amin/The Guardian

blocks.text: A community vigil was held for Haines in Wodonga on Wednesday evening after it was revealed the MP had lost both her legs following Monday’s alleged attack.
Haines’s predecessor as the federal member for Indi, Cathy McGowan, said on the sidelines of the event the community was grappling with “mixed emotions”.
McGowan had spent time with Haines’s staff and she told Guardian Australia they were “all crying together because of the emotion that’s been building up”.
“The people here tonight don’t want violence … but that’s not to say when violence happens in their communities they know what to do about it,” McGowan said.
“There’s a lot of violence in our communities, there’s a lot of violence online … there’s nothing new about this.
“What the attack on Helen has brought to our mind is, this is us. We can’t just pretend that everything’s OK in the regions and we’re doing fine.

articles.title: DFA: Chinese Embassy's recent remarks undermine efforts on bilateral relations
articles.summary: The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) on Thursday called out the Chinese Embassy in Manila for its recent social media posts, which the agency said affect mutual trust and confidence and severely…

blocks.text: Published October 22, 2026 9:58am

The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) on Thursday called out the Chinese Embassy in Manila for its recent social media posts, which the agency said affect mutual trust and confidence and severely undermine efforts to stabilize bilateral relations between the Philippines and China.
In a statement, the DFA said the social media posts of the Chinese Embassy were using “undiplomatic tone” which are not conducive to good relations.

“The escalatory and undiplomatic tone and language used in the latest social media statements of the Chinese Embassy erode mutual trust and confidence, and severely undermines the efforts to stabilize and improve bilateral relations,” the DFA said.

“The recent public statements of the Embassy do not reflect the longstanding spirit of constructive engagement between the two countries and the two foreign ministries. Such statements are not conducive to good relations nor to the effective discharge of diplomatic functions,” it added.
The Chinese Embassy has been posting and reacting on Facebook on of the statements of Philippine government officials and lawmakers who have been critical of them.
This came after Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan was condemned after he was quoted as saying that Beijing may easily win if it wants to use force against the Philippines.
The DFA thus reminded all diplomats accredited to the Philippines to exercise restraint and responsibility in their public statements, such as those posted on social media.
“All diplomats are expected to conduct and express themselves in a manner befitting diplomatic envoys, especially on social media,” it said.
The DFA also reiterated that it reserves the right to take further diplomatic action as it deems necessary.
Regardless, the agency said the Philippines continues to adhere to the One China Policy, anchored on the 1975 Philippines-China Joint Communique.

“It underscores our consistent position that the People’s Republic of China is the sole legal government of China, and that we fully understand and respect the position of the Chinese Government that there is but one China and that Taiwan is an integral part of Chinese territory,” the DFA said.
“Throughout the years, the Philippines’ relevant regulations reflect the country’s unwavering implementation of its One China Policy,” it added. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: US orders some diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia amid Houthi threat
articles.summary: The US State Department has asked some US diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia because of the threat of Houthi attacks on the Gulf kingdom.

image.caption: Houthis have attacked several major Saudi airports, including the capital Riyadh's King Khalid Airport [FILE: Oct 8, 2026]Image: Social Media/REUTERS

blocks.text: At least one person was killed in a strike on a Saudi airport in the eastern city of Dammam on Wednesday, as Washington ordered some diplomats and family members to leave the Gulf country.
Saudi Arabia's revived war with the Iranian-backed Houthi rebels has intensified in recent weeks, with the Yemeni rebels targeting several major Saudi airports.
Saudi Arabia on the backfoot in the war against the Houthis
What do we know about the strike on the airport in Dammam?
The Saudi Civil Aviation Authority said a strike on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam on Wednesday evening killed one person and injured eight others.
The authority added on X that the extent of the material damage to the airport was being assessed.
It did not say who was behind the attack and the Houthis did not claim responsibility.
Flight-tracking website Flightradar24 said flights from the airport were being diverted as operations came to a halt.

Earlier on Wednesday, the Saudi Energy Ministry said forces successfully intercepted a drone targeting an oil facility, but that falling debris killed two people and injured two others. Those killed were identified by the ministry as a Filipino and a Nepali national.
US State Department orders partial evacuation of Saudi mission
Meanwhile, US State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said his department had issued an order for the departure of non-essential staff and family members at the US embassy in Riyadh.

"Iranian-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions," Pigott wrote on X.
Both Reuters and AFP news agencies cited unnamed sources as saying a similar order was also issued for other countries in the Gulf, with AFP listing the UAE, Jordan, Qatar and Bahrain.
Pigott denied the reports, saying they were "inaccurate" and that only employees in Saudi Arabia were ordered to leave.
The US has issued similar evacuation orders on more than one occasion this year amid the Iran war and Iranian strikes on Saudi Arabia in retaliation for the US-Israeli war against Tehran.
Houthi attacks on Saudi airports raise stakes for Washington
A four-year truce between Saudi Arabia and the Houthi rebels collapsed amid the Iran war, with Saudi Arabia experiencing near daily attacks this month.

articles.title: ‘Almost looks fake’: two Sydney beaches closed after whale carcass washes up
articles.summary:
Swimming banned at Maroubra and Coogee while council prioritises ‘culturally respectful’ removal of remains

Coogee and Maroubra beaches have been closed as a precaution after a whale carcass…

blocks.text: Coogee and Maroubra beaches have been closed as a precaution after a whale carcass washed up on the rocks between the two busy swimming and surfing spots in Sydney’s eastern suburbs.

The local council said it was working with rangers and the New South Wales Department of Primary Industries on the whale’s removal from a “difficult-to-access location surrounded by cliffs and rock ledge”.

“As a precaution, Maroubra and Coogee Beach will remain closed until further notice while lifeguards monitor the situation and work with local stakeholders and authorities to arrange the whale’s removal,” Randwick council said.
The council said it was considering closing the surrounding area and rock shelf walkway to manage crowds on the popular coastal walk.

blocks.caption: The council is encouraging residents and visitors to avoid the area and follow directions from lifeguards. Composite: Randwick City Council

blocks.text: “At this stage, the carcass is not being removed and discussions are ongoing with the Gamay Rangers about a culturally and environmentally sensitive approach to take.”
The mayor, Dr Clare Willington, said the council would ensure that the removal was “culturally respectful” to Indigenous Australians.
“The whale is an important totem animal to the local Bidjigal people,” she said.
“This is a natural occurrence and in time nature will deal with the carcass. Our focus is to manage and limit any impact to swimmers and surfers at nearby beaches.”
The council is encouraging residents and visitors to avoid the area and follow directions from lifeguards and authorities.
It comes as authorities are working to free a large whale found stuck in shallow waters off off Turners Beach on Tasmania’s north-west coast.
“Members of the public are asked to avoid the area and not enter the water on the incoming tide due to the anticipated danger,” Tasmanian police said.
‘Almost looks fake’
Curious locals have stopped by Lurline Bay throughout the morning to try catch a glimpse of the whale.
Meeri Pajala, an au pair from Finland who is living in Sydney, said she had never seen anything like this before.
after newsletter promotion
“It almost looks fake to me,” she told Guardian Australia.
“That skin looks so weird.”
Glenda, a local who did not want her full name published, says she usually watches whales swimming by the coast and was curious when she heard the news.
“My interest is in if it’s newborn, or if it’s juvenile,” she said
“I thought it would be more complete.”
The carcass is relatively small and significantly deteriorated, with what appear to be bite marks along the blubber.
It was nudging up against the rocks as the waves ebbed and flowed but has become stuck in a crevice due to low tide.
To the surprise of many onlookers, it doesn’t seem to have a smell.
Authorities are still determining what species it is, and how the carcass arrived in the bay but it is believed to have died some time ago.

articles.title: Canadian publisher Boréal ends relationship with novelist Thélyson Orélien over alleged use of AI
articles.summary:
Author withdrawn from France’s Prix Goncourt last month has repeatedly denied using artificial intelligence to write novel

The publisher of top-selling Haitian Canadian writer Thélyson…

blocks.text: The publisher of top-selling Haitian Canadian writer Thélyson Orélien, who was removed from France’s most prestigious literary prize list last month, has confirmed the author used artificial intelligence to help write his novel C’était ça ou mourir (It Was Either That or Die).
Orélien has denied allegations that he used AI on his breakthrough novel and, last week, Canadian publisher Les Éditions du Boréal said it was standing by the 38-year-old writer.
But on Wednesday, Boréal said it had conducted a further investigation into the allegations.
“New information, confirmed over the past few days, indicates that artificial intelligence was used in the writing process” of the novel, a statement from Boréal said.
The publisher announced it was “ending its professional relationship” with Orélien.
Boréal said it did not know the extent of AI’s use in the writing process “and we will likely never have a definitive answer”.
It said it gathered all the working versions of the novel and hired an outside party to analyse various drafts.
“The results obtained this week revealed traces of AI tags in the metadata of certain documents,” Boréal said.
Before conducting this analysis, the publisher said it had tried to work with Orélien to gather the evidence necessary to prove his innocence.
That effort was inconclusive, and Orélien “subsequently announced that he would not provide any further information,” the publisher said.
The novel about migration had been scheduled for translation in more than 20 countries.

The book was shrouded in suspicion and withdrawn from the list for France’s book prize the Prix Goncourt, after tests with AI detector Pangram indicated a 100% probability it contained computer-generated text.
In a statement to Agence France-Presse earlier this month, Orélien called the allegations “slander and heresy”.
“Here and there I did use tools for research, particularly for foreign idioms,” he said in a statement sent exclusively to AFP.
“But not a single sentence in this book was created by a machine, nor the meaning or the structure of a story that comes from my gut.”
He stood firm on Wednesday, telling the French newspaper Libération he used AI “in the creative process” for “historical research”.
“I’ve explained everything to those close to me, but at the moment I don’t think my words count for anything,” he said, adding that what he is now experiencing has “gone way too far”.

Orélien said he started writing the book in late 2017 “on the corner of a table” and completed a first draft in 2019 of more than 300 pages, several years before the advent of AI services such as ChatGPT.
The author fled his native Haiti after a 2010 earthquake that struck the Caribbean island, already ravaged by poverty and unrest.
In response to separate allegations of plagiarism, Orélien admitted to making “unacceptable mistakes” in the past in his writing, without mentioning specifics.
“I was just over 20, I was probably a little too impatient, without really understanding how much I still had to learn. I wanted to write, I was reading a lot,” he wrote.
“But admiring someone does not give you the right to take, to claim as mine texts that are not my own.”

blocks.text: British Columbia·Updated
Vancouver Coastal Health (VCH) said in a Wednesday advisory that anyone who had contact with a "sick or abnormally behaving" skunk between Sept. 22 and Oct. 17 should seek treatment.
Vancouver Coastal Health is asking for downtown and West End residents to seek care if they had contact
A "small number" of people in the downtown Vancouver area have received treatment after being bitten by a skunk that tested positive for rabies, officials say.
Vancouver Coastal Health (VCH) said in a Wednesday advisory that the skunk was captured, and interactions with the animals are usually rare.
However, anyone who had contact with a "sick or abnormally behaving" skunk between Sept. 22 and Oct. 17 is being asked to seek treatment.
The area covered by the advisory includes Stanley Park and a chunk of downtown Vancouver and the West End, bordered by Georgia and Burrard streets.
Officials say the rabies virus is found in the saliva of infected animals and is usually transmitted through a bite, though it is less commonly transmitted through scratches.
Anyone who had contact with a sick skunk in the highlighted area of downtown Vancouver, which includes Stanley Park, is asked to seek treatment. (Vancouver Coastal Health)
West End resident Guerric Haché told CBC News that he caught the skunk in question last Saturday, when he was on his way to the West End Farmers' Market, at the corner of Comox and Bute streets.
He said a number of people were looking into the bushes nearby, and that's when he saw the animal, which looked lethargic and confused.
"I just started talking to the skunk because I'm an animal person. I like to do that," Haché said.
"I was saying, 'Hi, buddy, how you doing?' And the skunk looked up at me, and turned toward me, and it walked on to the sidewalk and it bit my leg and then it bit my shoe."
Haché captured the skunk and called an animal rescue charity, which subsequently sent the animal for tests, confirming it had rabies. (Submitted by Guerric Haché)
Haché said he called his partner, who helped him capture the skunk, and he sought medical care after calling an animal rescue charity to take the animal away.
Later, the West End resident says he was told the skunk had to be killed due to a broken jaw — and after it was tested, he got a call from VCH confirming it had rabies.
"There's only been three reported cases of rabies in skunks [in B.C.] since 2011, including this one. So it's extremely rare in B.C.," Haché said.
"So I thought there was a very small chance of it having rabies, and I knew that even if it did, it's extremely preventable. So I wasn't scared."

items: Multiple people treated after rabies found in skunk in Kootenay Lake region of B.C.

blocks.text: Haché said several people stopped by as he waited for animal rescue workers to arrive, describing how they had heard there was an aggressive skunk in the neighbourhood.

He said it was concerning that a skunk with rabies could have been around, but it demonstrated the importance of letting public health authorities know if an animal is behaving aggressively or looking confused, because it could mean the animal is ill.
"Rabies virus is not transmitted through exposure to the spray, urine or feces of infected skunks," the VCH advisory reads.
VCH says rabies is a serious infection that can affect the brain and nervous system, and they are extremely rare in Canada.
"Infections are fatal but can be prevented when rabies vaccines and/or rabies immunoglobulin are administered promptly after an exposure," the advisory reads.

A skunk is seen in a stock image. Vancouver Coastal Health says a small number of people have received treatment after being bitten by a rabid skunk in the downtown area. (Fiona M. Donnelly/Shutterstock)
It adds that bats are the only known "reservoirs" of rabies in B.C., which means they spread it to another animals, and occasionally other animals like skunks in specific areas get the disease.
"If you are bitten or scratched by a bat, skunk or any wild animal, wash the wound with soap and warm water for at least 15 minutes and seek medical care immediately," the VCH advisory reads.
Any downtown Vancouver pet owners whose animal had direct contact with a skunk during the four weeks identified by authorities should contact their vet immediately, according to VCH.

articles.title: Some US diplomats told to leave Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks
articles.summary:
Reports emerge of similar withdrawals in UAE, Jordan, Qatar and Bahrain amid concerns about a return to conflict with Iran after US midterm elections

The US state department has ordered some…

blocks.text: The US state department has ordered some diplomats and the families of US government employees to leave Saudi Arabia, as the gulf kingdom faces a barrage of near-daily attacks, with at least three people killed at an airport and oilfield on Wednesday evening.

Attacks on “civilian airports and other critical infrastructure” by the Iranian-supported Houthis in Yemen were highlighted as the reason for the drawdown. State department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said: “The safety and security of department personnel and their families remain our highest priority.”

The state department said the order covered its embassy in Riyadh and its satellite consulates. The embassy had been badly damaged at the start of the US war on Iran and had been operating with only a skeleton staff for months, although in recent weeks some diplomats had returned.

The announcement comes as some media – including NBC and AFP – reported that families of US embassy personnel were also being withdrawn from the United Arab Emirates, Jordan, Qatar and Bahrain, while the New York Times said the Trump administration was developing plans to restart the war on Iran.

However in his statement on Wednesday, Pigott described the reports of further withdrawals as “inaccurate” and stressed that the state department order was for the departure of staff and their families from Saudi Arabia only.

Saudi Arabia has faced a succession of deadly attacks from the Houthis over recent weeks, including a strike on Riyadh’s international airport that was the kingdom’s deadliest in years, as the war with the group escalates.
On Wednesday evening the Saudi Civil Aviation Authority announced that one Saudi resident was killed in attacks on King Fahad international airport in Dammam, on the Gulf near Bahrain and Qatar.

Eight people were injured and the airport also suffered some material damage, according to officials. Global flight-tracking service Flightradar24 said flights had been diverted away from the airport.

Separately, falling debris from the successful interception of a drone targeting an oil facility in the country’s south-east also killed two people and injured a further two, the Saudi energy ministry said.

Neither attack was immediately claimed by the Houthis, but airports and oil facilities have been a major target of the militant group in their recent wave of missile and projectile strikes on Saudi Arabia.

The US previously ordered non-essential staff to leave the Gulf ahead of the start of its war against Iran in late February. NBC reported that the US military has been quietly scaling back its presence at bases across the Middle East in recent days, however a spokesperson from US central command told the US outlet that service members are regularly moved to “optimize mission readiness”.
The withdrawal of staff from the region comes amid reports that Trump has been presented with plans for restarting strikes on Iran, after the midterm elections.

The New York Times reported that the US and Israel developed plans for a “short but intensive operation”, after defense secretary Peter Hegseth travelled to Israel earlier this week for meetings with prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Last week ⁠Trump said the US was looking to knock out Iran’s Pickaxe Mountain, a site linked to the country’s ⁠nuclear program, however the president has publicly said that he does not intend to restart the war before the 3 November elections.
With Reuters and Agence France-Presse

articles.title: Lawmakers hail Supreme Court ruling voiding billions in budget items
articles.summary: Lawmakers have welcomed the Supreme Court's ruling declaring key provisions of the 2024, 2025 and 2026 General Appropriations Acts (GAA) unconstitutional, describing the decision as a decisive…

blocks.text: October 22, 2026 | 8:09am
The logo of the Supreme Court at the Supreme Court Building in Manila.
Philstar.com / Ian Laqui

MANILA, Philippines — Lawmakers have welcomed the Supreme Court's ruling declaring key provisions of the 2024, 2025 and 2026 General Appropriations Acts (GAA) unconstitutional, describing the decision as a decisive victory for public accountability.

The high court’s 121-page decision, released to the press on October 20, invalidated congressional increases totaling P449.5 billion in 2024 unprogrammed appropriations, a P17.99-billion addition to the 2025 Special Road Fund, and key provisions governing 2026 standby funds.
The court ruled that Congress committed a grave abuse of discretion by exceeding the constitutional cap on the executive’s total recommended appropriations.
Sen. Panfilo Lacson lauded the ruling's timing as the Senate prepares to review the House version of the 2027 General Appropriations Bill.

"One good thing about the Supreme Court ruling is its timing. It couldn’t have come at a better time when the House version of the 2027 General Appropriations Bill is undergoing scrutiny by the Senate," Lacson said.

Lacson, who was not a member of the Senate when the 2024 and 2025 national budgets were passed, warned of imminent friction between the two legislative chambers as the Senate addresses "red flags" in the proposed 2027 spending plan.

He indicated that the Senate may restore hundreds of billions of pesos in cuts and realignments introduced by the House, particularly regarding Foreign-Assisted Projects (FAPs) and flood control allocations.

Describing the ruling's historical impact, Lacson asserted that the 2024 and 2025 national budgets would "go down in history as the worst budgets ever passed by Congress," comparing their invalidation to the Supreme Court's landmark decision striking down the Disbursement Acceleration Program (DAP) under the 2013 GAA.
On the immediate practical consequences of the decision, Lacson clarified that funds remaining unspent may no longer be disbursed, while those already expended cannot be invalidated retroactively.
Sen. Leila de Lima, who served as a co-petitioner in the consolidated legal challenges against the 2026 unprogrammed appropriations, hailed the ruling as a major triumph in curbing fiscal abuse.
"This decision of the Supreme Court is a warning to those who conspire and plan to abuse Unprogrammed Appropriations for personal and political interests," De Lima said in Filipino.

"Starting with the 2022 GAA, the unprogrammed funds were growing out of control. It became a holding area for pork, where lawmakers could park projects, create artificial fiscal space, and redirect hundreds of billions to their pet allocations. The Supreme Court has closed that backdoor,” she added.

articles.title: A Glee reboot is officially happening, and fans are buzzing
articles.summary: Gleeks, ready your slushies — the wacky, irreverent musical dramedy that broke barriers and launched careers in the 2010s is officially getting a reboot, and several original cast members have…

image.caption: A reboot is on the way for the 2010s show Glee. And several members of the original cast, seen here in 2010 performing a concert at the Dodge Theatre in Phoenix, are hinting they're coming back for it. (Ross D. Franklin/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New

Gleeks, ready your slushies — the wacky, irreverent musical dramedy that broke barriers and launched careers in the 2010s is officially getting a reboot, and several original cast members have indicated they’re coming back for the ride.
Hints that Lea Michele, Heather Morris and Kevin McHale are returning
The official Instagram for Glee posted confirmation of a reboot on Wednesday with a picture that says, “It’s official, Glee is returning,” and the caption: “Currently gleeking out!”
Disney+ and Hulu, reportedly handling the reboot, were both tagged as creators on the post.

The original show ran on Fox from 2009 to 2015 and followed a ragtag group of students in the William McKinley High School show choir as they tackled issues like relationships, sexuality, identity, or what to do when a rival show choir nearly blinds you by putting rock salt in a slushie they throw in your face (yes, that was a real plotline on Glee).
While the reunion can't be complete since three original cast members have died, several actors from the first show have publicly alluded to involvement with the reboot.
Lea Michele, who first came to fame playing Rachel Berry in the show, is reportedly coming back to the show, according to Variety, with one source telling the outlet, “she’s in.”
Heather Morris shared a throwback photo of herself as her Glee character, cheerleader Brittany Pierce, on Instagram on Wednesday, adding that the character is "back for more."

Other cast members have hinted at being involved. Former castmate Chord Overstreet posted, “Reunited and it feels so good!” on X on Wednesday. Kevin McHale, who played Artie Abrams, shared a 2020 post about Drake surpassing the cast of Glee for the most Billboard Hot 100 hits of all time, adding the reaction, “Challenge accepted.”

McHale previously expressed enthusiasm to People Magazine in September, saying, “If someone like Ryan [Murphy] is willing to get all of us in a room and on a set together, I could never say no to that. I love all of those people.”

“I’ve been in touch with around 10 of the original cast members,” Murphy said in an interview with Entertainment Tonight at the end of September, adding that he’d already written a script for the reboot. “They all were very enthusiastic about the idea.”

The internet is buzzing already. Comments under the show’s announcement on Instagram range from shock — “Ur kidding,” singer Laufey posted — to excitement, to horror. “As a huge Glee fan, this is a terrible idea,” one user wrote.
CBC News has reached out to Disney+ and Hulu for comment.
The legacy of Glee

The show’s music was wildly successful, with 207 songs charting on the Billboard Hot 100 during its run. For its first couple of seasons, the show was also a critical and commercial darling, with fans connecting to its message of misfits finding a sense of belonging, and praising its representation.
A Slate article about the show’s finale suggested that the show “did more to normalize homosexuality than any other show in TV history, perhaps more than any other mainstream work of art.”

Cast members Darren Criss, left, and Chris Colfer pose at the Paley Center for Media's PaleyFest 2011 event honouring the television series Glee at the Saban Theatre in Los Angeles on March 16, 2011. (Mario Anzuoni/Reuters)

But the show was also criticized for how its wildly teetering tone, ricocheting at times from satire to painfully sincere, meant some serious topics such as bullying and eating disorders were trivialized.

Tragedy and scandal also surrounded the production and its cast both during the show and in the years after. Cory Monteith, who played the show’s star quarterback, Finn Hudson, died in Vancouver of an accidental overdose in 2013 at the age of 31, while the show was still airing. Mark Salling, who played Puck, died by suicide after pleading guilty in 2017 to possessing child pornography.
And star Naya Rivera, beloved for her portrayal of Santana on the show, died in an accidental drowning in 2020, after saving her son.
A controversial 2023 docuseries by Investigation Discovery called The Price of Glee claimed to investigate a “curse” behind the show, but was denounced by multiple members of the cast.

In this Jan. 13, 2018, file photo, Naya Rivera participates in the Step Up: High Water panel during the YouTube Television Critics Association Winter Press Tour in Pasadena, Calif. (Willy Sanjuan/Invision/The Associated Press)

Michele was also accused in 2020 of engaging in bullying and racist remarks on the set of the show by former Glee co-star Samantha Ware. Other castmates came forward to share similar experiences, and Michele publicly apologized for her behaviour.
Despite the show's complicated backstory, the internet is reeling at the news that this onetime cultural phenomenon is coming back.

“Just heard the news, I’m trembling,” TikTok influencer @Max_Balegde said in a video. He speculated with excitement that the reboot would probably feature at least one Chappell Roan cover, and then said, “I hope Sue Sylvester does a Katseye song.”
Jane Lynch, who played the endlessly meme-able Coach Sue Sylvester, hasn’t confirmed that she’s reprising the role, but did share an article about the reboot on her Instagram story on Wednesday.

Influencer Chris Olsen shared a TikTok of him reacting with shock under text reading “WHAT DO YOU MEAN IT’S OFFICIALLY COMING BACK???” as the Glee cover of River Deep, Mountain High played in the background.
Not every fan is confident that a reboot could capture the original chaotic feeling of the show.

In September, TikTok user @sammnnicole posted a compilation of some of the stranger moments of Glee, with the text "the Glee reboot could never recreate this masterpiece" over it. The video, which has more than 350,000 views, included a moment from Season 3 in which the Glee cast dove into a pool one by one while singing Rihanna’s We Found Love — with McHale’s Artie cheerfully rolling his wheelchair into the water at the end.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Alexandra Mae Jones is a senior writer for CBC News based in Toronto. She has written on a variety of topics, from health to pop culture to breaking news, and previously reported for CTV News and the Toronto Star. She joined CBC in 2024. You can reach her at alexandra.mae.jones@cbc.ca

articles.title: The real reasons US politicians are getting older
articles.summary: No country for young men and women: why do older politicians seem to have such a tight grip on the US political system?

blocks.text: Twenty-seven-year-old Republican Riley Owen is one of the few candidates from Gen Z - aged in their early teens to late 20s - from either party running for Congress on 3 November.

Owen is running in a newly created district in Utah that experts say may lean towards the Democrats. He has championed issues including paid maternity leave, restrictions on congressional stock trading and environmental action - all issues that may appeal to Democratic supporters.

When he was confirmed as his party's candidate in the state's 1st congressional district, he walked on stage to Billy Joel's We Didn't Start the Fire, and argued that his generation needed to help renew the American Dream.

The gerontocracy is "a bipartisan issue", he says. "We've got people who have become career politicians, and they spend their lives in Congress." He says this is indicative of a system that is not delivering for Americans.
Owen says the big challenge he faces is the fact that money really talks in US politics. Research suggests campaign donors tend to prefer incumbent candidates.

Indeed, the campaign of his rival Ben McAdams - a 51-year-old Democrat who has previously served in Congress - has so far raised much more cash than Owen's. By mid-October, McAdams had raised over $2.6m (£1.9m), compared with $150,000 raised by Owen, according to records on the Federal Election Commission website.

Owen argues that his generation is uniquely well-placed to understand contemporary political issues, such as the challenges posed by tech. He also disputes any suggestion that a younger candidate necessarily lacks relevant experience - pointing to his own background as a military officer and a White House policy analyst. "I think in politics, just like in industry, we need what's called disruptive innovation," he says.

The age of America's top politicians has long been a talking point. In 1984 Reagan - who was then America's oldest president at age 73 - deflected scrutiny with a quip about the "youth and inexperience" of his opponent Walter Mondale, who was a sprightly 56.

In the US, individual states also have their own legislatures, with a Senate and a House, where many politicians make their start. Many current members of Congress spent years in state politics before running for a seat in Washington

For those young people who do end up in high-profile political positions, the next question is whether they can make a success of it, especially when it comes to parenthood. Over the summer, the stories of two high-profile young women working in Washington raised fresh questions around compatibility of the job with motherhood.
Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, 37, a Democratic congresswoman who took office aged 29, announced that she had started the process of freezing her eggs.

Later the same week in August, Karoline Leavitt, 29, who was appointed the youngest ever White House press secretary almost two years earlier, said she would leave the Trump administration to spend more time with her family, including her newborn baby. She explained: "I cannot be the best mom my two young children deserve while devoting the constant time, energy and attention required of [being] the White House press secretary."

Only a handful of women have given birth while elected to Congress, while a few dozen lawmakers are mothers to children under the age of 18. The federal government, like many US employers, does not offer paid parental leave.

JD Vance, 42, one of the youngest vice-presidents in US history, recently acknowledged that having young children might impact on his own decision to run for the White House in 2028, saying: "We've got four little kids."

articles.title: Pope Leo will not need further cancer treatment — Vatican
articles.summary: Pope Leo's lung cancer surgery last week was a success, the Vatican said. The pope broke with traditions of secrecy around papal health issues after announcing he needed surgery to remove a nodule on…

image.caption: The 71-year-old pontiff thanked worshippers for their prayers during the weekly general audience at St. Peter's Square at the VaticanImage: Tiziana Fabi/AFP

blocks.text: Pope Leo XIV will not require further cancer treatment, his doctors announced on Wednesday, after the pontiff was diagnosed with lung cancer last week.
The Vatican cited the pope's doctors, Dr. Luigi Carbone and Professor Stefano Margaritora, as saying the pope's disease was localized and that "no further treatment" was necessary.
This confirms earlier prognoses suggesting the pope's cancer was caught early.
Pope Leo last week underwent surgery to remove the lower lobe of his right lung on October 13 at Rome's Gemelli hospital.
What did Pope Leo's doctors say about his health condition?
The 71-year-old pontiff's doctors said the final histopathology and molecular testing reports on the tissue removed during his surgery were issued on Wednesday.

"The results confirmed that the tumor was a lung adenocarcinoma and that the disease was localized. A subsequent oncological assessment has confirmed that no further treatment is necessary," the Holy See said.
What to know about Pope Leo XIV's lung cancer
The pope's surgeon added that there was "no clinical reason to cancel" the pope's visit to South America.
The ambitious trip, initially scheduled for November 6-17, would take the pontiff to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, involving a dozen flights, two helicopter rides and stops at high altitude.
Pope Leo's transparency around illness breaks with tradition
Leo was discharged from the hospital on Saturday, saying he would resume his activities gradually.
His illness shocked the Catholic Church, stoking concern that any potential prolonged treatment, such as radiotherapy or chemotherapy, could have affected the pope's ability to head the church.
Pope Leo first announced his condition during the traditional Sunday blessing on October 11, telling followers that he would be having a nodule surgically removed.
The announcement broke away from long-held traditions of secrecy surrounding papal health issues.

articles.title: 'Rosal' slightly weakens; Batanes, Babuyan Islands under Signal No. 2
articles.summary: PAGASA said the center of Rosal's eye is estimated to be 495 kilometers east of Basco, Batanes.

blocks.text: October 22, 2026 | 7:15am
Satellite image from PAGASA showing Super Typhoon Rosal as of 4:40 a.m. on Oct. 22, 2026.
PAGASA / Released

MANILA, Philippines — Super Typhoon Rosal (international name: Champi) slightly weakened as it continued its northwestward track over the Philippine Sea east of Batanes, the state weather bureau PAGASA said.
As of 4 a.m. on Thursday, October 22, PAGASA said the center of Rosal's eye was estimated to be 495 kilometers east of Basco, Batanes.
Rosal now has maximum sustained winds of 195 kilometers per hour (kph) near the center and gusts of up to 240 kph, with a central pressure of 915 hPa.
It is moving northwestward at 20 kph, with Rosal’s strong to typhoon-force winds extending outward up to 780 kilometers from its center.

Despite its weakening, PAGASA maintained Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No. 2 in two areas, where estimated gale-force winds of 62 to 88 kph pose a minor to moderate threat to life and property within 24 hours:

items: Batanes
Northeastern portion of the Babuyan Islands

blocks.text: Meanwhile, Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No. 1 remains hoisted over the following localities, where strong winds of 39 to 61 kph are expected within 36 hours:

items: Babuyan Islands: Remaining portion
Cagayan: Mainland
Isabela: Eastern portion (Maconacon, Divilacan, Palanan, Santa Maria, Cabagan, Delfin Albano, Santo Tomas, Tumauini, San Pablo, Ilagan City, San Mariano, Dinapigue)
Ilocos Norte
Apayao

blocks.text: PAGASA noted that Signal No. 3 remains the highest warning level that may be raised over Batanes during Rosal's passage. However, should the typhoon shift to a more north-northwestward track, raising Signal No. 3 will become less likely.
Rosal entered the Philippine area of responsibility at 2 a.m., according to PAGASA.
Track forecast

Rosal is projected to continue moving northwestward until Friday morning, October 23. It will turn north-northwestward by Friday afternoon before recurving north-northeastward by Saturday, October 24.

The typhoon is expected to make its closest approach to Extreme Northern Luzon between Thursday afternoon and Friday morning. It is forecast to exit the Philippine area of responsibility (PAR) by Friday evening or early Saturday morning.
The state weather bureau expects Rosal to continue gradually weakening throughout the day, with a potential downgrade to typhoon status.
Rapid weakening is expected by Saturday, when the cyclone may be further downgraded to a severe tropical storm.

articles.title: German youth plan France-style mass protests
articles.summary: A youth-led movement in Germany has called for demonstrations in major cities of the country on October 31.

image.caption: A person carrying a placard that says "I want to live, not just survive" [FILE: December 2023]Image: Ying Tang/NurPhoto/picture alliance

blocks.text: "Gen Z regelt" — or Gen Z's Got It — a youth initiative, has called for mass protests in 21 cities across Germany on Saturday, October 31; including Berlin, Cologne, Hamburg and Munich.
Thousands are expected to participate in demonstrations protesting "broken schools and austerity," as well as the cost of living, social injustice, military conscription and climate change.

French protests that exploded in violence and rampant destruction of private and public property this weekend also grew out of student frustration over the national school system and soon included numerous unions, groups and individuals voicing anger over a number of issues.
Gen Z regelt's website clearly states that the initiative is "against all violence," whether directed at people or property.
Police say they are "vigilant and relaxed," adding that they intend to protect people's right to congregate and express their opinions.

Still, images of massive damage and public violence from France, Italy and Spain have raised concerns among domestic policymakers and police, who have warned against allowing the protests to be hijacked by left-wing extremists.

Andreas Roßkopf, head of the German Federal Police's GdP union, made clear that officers would deal harshly with riots and rioters, telling the Rheinische Post newspaper on Wednesday, "state, but also federal police, will offer a firm and decisive response" to any trouble.
Roßkopf also warned that radicals and extremists could insert themselves among demonstrators in order to "attack police" or "simply be destructive."

articles.title: Trump's green card curbs test Indian tech workers' American dream
articles.summary: With immigration curbs and tech firms cutting foreign hiring, US residency is becoming a distant dream for many Indians.

blocks.text: For millions of Indians, the road to the ultimate career aspiration had a familiar script - an engineering degree to get a tech services job, then a posting in the US, repeated visa renewals and then the green card that gave them permanent residency in the country.
But that may end soon.

Earlier this month, the US announced it would suspend eight technology firms, including Microsoft, India's Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro and HCL Technologies, from hiring skilled international workers on a permanent basis through a widely used visa pathway.

New and pending applications under the Permanent Labor Certification Program, or PERM, have been frozen. This is a big blow to Indians who hold a majority of H-1B visas - a temporary visa for specialists - which they used to work in the US while relying on PERM to get a green card and, ultimately, citizenship.

The latest announcement is in line with Trump's push for stricter skilled-worker immigration rules, which tech firms have been adapting to and, therefore, the impact on businesses may be minimal, experts say.
Nasscom, the trade association of India's $300bn (£226bn) technology industry, says that Indian companies have reduced the dependence on H-1B visas and are hiring more locally.
"Consequently, the number of employees transitioning from H-1B visas to permanent residency through the PERM process is also relatively limited," the association adds.

Wipro said in a statement that more than 80% of its workforce in the US is locally hired. Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), said its PERM applications were in single digits in the last two years. Microsoft said in a statement that it has filed for H-1B visas mostly to retain existing staff, not to import new workers.

A report in Business Standard newspaper, citing PERM Tracker, said, TCS' applications filings fell to two in 2025-26 from 513 in the previous year and 1,804 in the year before that. The report said no records were found for Infosys and Wipro for 2025-26.
BBC's email to all eight companies asking questions about the impact of the restriction and how they were supporting affected employees in the US remained unanswered.
Brokerage firm HDFC Securities said the impact on tech firms would be minimal, as PERM-linked jobs make up only a small share of revenue, even if higher-paid American workers replace them.
But the US government's decision has an impact beyond business.

A US-based senior executive with one of these eight firms told the BBC on condition of anonymity that the new PERM restriction will "not break the business", but the impact is more "intense" at a human level.

"A good number of people we know are stuck in a space where they have spent some years in the US but their green card application hasn't moved. Even if they are ready to move back to India, their children don't want to because they grew up here," he said.
Recent policy moves have deepened uncertainty and amplified online hostility towards Indian immigrants and H-1B visa holders.

Researchers at Stop AAPI Hate, a US non-profit that combats anti-Asian and Pacific Islander discrimination, have reported a sharp increase in anti-South Asian online sentiment since the 2024 US election, with Indian immigrants and H-1B visa holders being frequent targets.
While barring the eight tech companies from PERM, US Vice President JD Vance too referred to foreign professionals holding H-1B visas as "foreign indentured servants".

While he later acknowledged that it was an "imperfect" rhetoric, his remark drew sharp criticism from India's foreign ministry which called it "unwarranted" and "deeply offensive" for the colonial connotation.

Poorvi Chothani, founder and managing partner of global immigration law firm LawQuest, said many came to the US for better prospects, borrowing heavily to study and build careers. But as rules tighten now, they have fewer options and less ability to absorb the costs.
Immigration experts believe that as pathways for residency become limited, some may reconsider their future in the US, while others may choose not to move at all.
Ahmet Gulek, Postdoctoral Fellow at Stanford's Immigration Policy Lab, told BBC that despite alternate ways to get residency, not many may be feasible.
While moving to another firm not covered by the suspension is an option, he flags that it's unclear if those firms would be open to hiring immigrants given "the fear of retaliation".
Besides, it's also a tough time to change jobs.
The technology industry has already been reshaped by layoffs, cost-cutting and the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), making career moves tougher.

But there are other routes to a US green card. People with exceptional accomplishments or whose work advances national interests may be eligible for categories that bypass the PERM labour certification process.
Applicants can also qualify for permanent residency by investing at least $800,000 in eligible US enterprises.
Gulek warns some of these categories "may be targeted next."
While Chothani says some are so keen to stay in the US that they are considering the EB-5 investor route but may not have enough capital to invest.

Nearly one million Indian nationals were waiting for employment-based green cards as of December 2025, representing 79% of the total pending applications, according to the National Foundation for American Policy (NFAP).

Their report projects wait times ranging from five to 179 years for highly skilled Indians filing labour certification or employment-based immigration petitions from January 2026, depending on the visa category.

Like other recent immigration measures, the PERM suspension may face federal court challenges. But together, these moves signal a more restrictive climate for those hoping to study, work or settle in the US.

Earlier, the Trump administration imposed a $100,000 fee on certain new H-1B visa petitions, a measure that was later struck down by federal courts. More recently, it has also proposed a $70,000 fee for universities recommending international students for a programme that allows graduates to work in the country after completing their studies.

"This trend is not changing anytime soon," said an Indian professional, who spoke to BBC on condition of anonymity and has transitioned to an H-1B visa recently after a "long wait". He says both the Republican Party and the Democratic Party agree immigration laws need reform, even if they disagree on how.

Some research suggests that restrictions could shift jobs to India rather than to American workers. This is supported by industry players saying that they are already witnessing an increase in companies offshoring work.

"Companies benefit from cost arbitrage when they move work offshore. Post Covid, there is also greater acceptance and appreciation for remote work from clients," the executive from the tech firm earlier quoted says.

Experts believe America's appetite for Indian tech talent is unlikely to disappear. What may be changing is how it taps that talent. For Indian professionals, that could mean rewriting the script about building a future in the US.

articles.title: From The Matrix to Yaga, Carrie-Anne Moss still believes rejection can open the right door
articles.summary: Canadian actor Carrie-Anne Moss reflects on her path from Vancouver to The Matrix, and the experiences that shaped her acting career. She also discusses returning to British Columbia for Yaga,…

blocks.text: Carrie-Anne Moss seduces Hudson Williams in Yaga
Carrie-Anne Moss had just opened one of her favourite books to a chapter about Baba Yaga when an offer arrived to join the new series, Yaga.
The timing felt like a sign.

In an interview with CBC's Eli Glasner, Moss said she has owned Women Who Run with the Wolves: Myths and Stories of the Wild Woman Archetype by Clarissa Pinkola Estés since 1999, and the chapter's subject echoed the project in front of her.
"I take those kinds of things quite literally," Moss said. "Things like that have always guided my life."
Created by Canadian playwright Kat Sandler, Yaga is a dark mystery-thriller adapted from her 2019 stage play.

items: Toronto fans go wild for Hudson Williams. And the cast of his new show goes wild for Canada
Seana McKenna stars in Yaga, a 'socially conscious fairy tale' that expands on the aging woman archetype

blocks.text: Noah Reid (Schitt's Creek) stars as private investigator Charlie Rapp, who sets out to find missing heir Henry Park, played by Hudson Williams (Heated Rivalry). In the fictional coastal town of Whittock, the case begins to echo the Slavic legend of Baba Yaga — an enigmatic figure whose hut is said to stand on chicken legs, and whose intentions can be as unpredictable as her power.

Sandler sent Moss a letter explaining why she wanted her for the role of Katherine Hargrove, a professor drawn to younger men. Moss read the letter, Sandler's pitch and the scripts before deciding to take the part.
Carrie-Anne Moss stars as Prof. Katherine Hargrove in the mystery-thriller series, Yaga. (Christopher Lawrence/Crave)
Filming in Victoria has brought Moss back to British Columbia, where she grew up. She used to spend summers on the island with her aunt and uncle, helping care for their children.
'I always wanted to be an actress'

Moss grew up in Burnaby and later lived with her mother in Granville Island while attending high school. She remembers taking the bus on her own to see the school plays, musicals and performing arts group that toured Vancouver and gave her early chances to perform.
"I always wanted to be an actress," she told CBC News. Watching television helped spark that ambition. Moss said she felt deeply invested in the shows and the emotions they stirred in her.
"I'm crying because of what they're doing, I'm laughing because of what they're doing. Like, I want to do that."
Acting felt less like a calculated career plan than a purpose she had found early, Moss said. She sang in choirs, wrote plays and musicals — she loved performing.
"It was actually very innocent and beautiful," Moss said.
"I hope for that kind of desire in someone's soul … to feel that that's your purpose."
Moss attends a promotional event for the television series Models Inc. on June 24, 1994 in Santa Monica, Calif. (Ron Galella, Ltd./Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images)
Move to L.A. 'not always easy,' she says
That ambition took Moss from Vancouver to Toronto, where she worked as a model, and then to Europe.

While living in Barcelona, she landed her first major role on the television series Dark Justice (1991-93), a crime drama about a judge who moonlights as a vigilante. Moss played the judge's legal clerk Tara McDonald.
When the show moved to Los Angeles, Moss went with it.

That move was difficult. Moss said she had little money, few friends and no green card, which meant securing a visa whenever she worked. She rented a room from comedian Pat Bullard, the ex-husband of her manager at the time, and relied on the opportunities that came her way.
Still, she never considered going home. Moss said she had asked herself whether her desire to act came from ego or a wish to be famous, and concluded it was a genuine calling.
"I believed that with the purity of that intention that it would open for me," she said. "It was not always easy."
That belief was tested when she was let go from a television series after two seasons. The rejection hurt and left Moss questioning what came next.

By 1997, Moss was auditioning for the role that would change her career. Her final screen test for Trinity in The Matrix took place that August — on her 30th birthday — with Keanu Reeves, who was recovering from neck surgery and wearing a brace.

Moss went through several callbacks but didn't expect to land what would become her breakout role of Trinity. Her agent cautioned her not to get too excited. She said she chose to celebrate each audition as it came, treating the opportunity as something worth appreciating on its own.
When the call finally came, she told CBC News, "I think I fell to my knees."
Looking back, Moss sees the television rejection as what made the audition possible. She said the experience has also shaped how she talks with her children about disappointment.

"When one door closes you have to trust it," she said. "You can feel your feelings, cry about it, be upset about it. But you have to know that you will look back and you will say that was meant to be."
Moss 'cried' 1st time she watched The Matrix

Preparing for The Matrix meant four months of martial arts training alongside Keanu Reeves, Laurence Fishburne and Hugo Weaving. The intense preparation brought the cast close, Moss said, and she came to think of them as her "family."
Still, she couldn't picture how the film's camera movements, colour and composition would come together until she saw the finished movie.

items: Carrie-Anne Moss on The Matrix and her new horror film about a zombie-like pandemic
Keanu Reeves, Carrie-Anne Moss to return in new Matrix film

blocks.text: "The first time I saw it, I cried," she said.
It was difficult, at first, to watch herself on the big screen. It took a few viewings before she could look past her own performance and take in the film as a whole.

The role made Moss an international name. Since then, she has appeared in films including Memento (2000), Chocolat (2000) and Snow Cake (2006) and returned to the franchise in 2021's The Matrix Resurrections.
She has also stepped away from work at times to raise her children. "I have loved raising my children more than anything. ... It was really a no-brainer for me."
Moss, centre, and sons Owen Roy, left, and Kaden Roy, right, attend a Star Wars premiere in Los Angeles on Dec. 9, 2017. (Presley Ann/Patrick McMullan via Getty Images)
Moss and her family now live in New Hampshire, after decades in Los Angeles. She said she wanted a quieter life — and to "see the stars at night."
Moss not a fan of AI

But leaving Hollywood hasn't meant the leaving the creative world. Moss said she's thinking about the future of her work and the role of human creativity, and she's concerned about what artificial intelligence could mean for artists and storytelling.
"Not a fan," Moss said. She adds that using AI in her own writing can make her feel as if part of her creativity shuts off.

items: Could AI really 'kill all humans'? Breaking down the dire warnings about the technology's existential risk
Celebrities are telling women to use more AI or be 'left behind.' Their followers aren't having it

blocks.text: Moss said she tries not to let fear take over.
She said she sees storytelling as a way to build empathy and connection. She also said the changes brought by AI raise deeper questions about what people value and what they might lose.
"I feel it's a spiritual battle, personally," she said.
For now, she is focused on the choices in front of her — including a return to the province where she grew up, and a role that seemed to find her at just the right time.

articles.title: Vance tells Republicans to 'stop whining' about controversial Ohio attack ad
articles.summary: The ad by Ohio Republican Vivek Ramaswamy features his Democratic rival's estranged mother, who she has not seen since her stepfather was charged with sexual abuse in her childhood.

blocks.text: US Vice-President JD Vance has urged fellow Republicans to stop "whining" about a controversial attack ad that featured a Democratic candidate's estranged mother calling her a liar.
While campaigning in Ohio for Vivek Ramaswamy, the Republican candidate for governor, Vance said he was "a little bit disgusted" by criticism from members of his own party.

In the ad, Donna Arthur, the mother of Democratic candidate Amy Acton, said her daughter "lied her entire life". It does not mention that Arthur's husband was charged with raping Acton when she was a child.
The Ramaswamy campaign have claimed credit for the ad, and have paid millions to have it advertised around the state.
Acton's brother is among those who have condemned the ad, saying turning alleged sexual assault into "a political talking point" was a "despicable low".
Acton and her brother were removed from their mother's custody when her stepfather, Cledith Arthur, was arrested and charged in 1978.

That is when she last spoke to her mother, Acton said in an interview with The Vindicator, an Ohio news outlet. The Arthurs fled Ohio and Cledith Arthur was never prosecuted on the rape charge. He died in 2004.

When the ad featuring Donna Arthur was initially released to social media on Monday evening, it did not say who the video was paid for or authorised by. Ramaswamy confirmed on Tuesday that it came from his campaign, and he later pledged to spend $4m (£2.9m) to further air it.
The move has drawn a bipartisan backlash.
Former South Carolina Governor Nikki Haley, who ran against Ramaswamy for the Republican nomination for president in 2024, said "he's a bad guy. It's a shame he continues to get away with it".
Vance, when asked by BBC News if he thought the ad was appropriate, answered: "It's not really my concern."
"What is my concern is who's going to govern the next generation of American government."

He also said he was "a little bit disgusted" by members of his own party who "are whining more about that advertisement than they are about what the congressional Democrats and other Democrats want to do to the United States of America".

Vance, a former Ohio senator, later defended the ad at a rally for Ramaswamy, saying: "Now the media and the Democrats in the state of Ohio are obsessed because guess what? Vivek Ramaswamy had the audacity to run a TV commercial which calls it out like it is, and calls Amy Acton a liar."
When asked about Ramaswamy's ad on Wednesday, Trump said: "I know nothing about it. I heard the mother went very rogue on the daughter."
He added: "It's a very unusual situation to have a mother hate a daughter that much. But I dont think that has anything to do with Vivek."
Acton's team released its own campaign ad on Tuesday, a video featuring her brother, Philip Stearns, recounting childhood abuse and saying "Amy always got the worst of it".
"Shame on Vivek," he says in the 30-second clip. "It's the contempt he has for Amy. It's the contempt he has for Ohio."
Other Republicans, including ones running for statewide office, have now criticised the ad.
Ohio Senator John Husted, who is up for re-election, told the Associated Press: "I would not have run that ad."
Ohio Secretary of Frank LaRose, who is running to be state auditor, was another Republican coming out against the ad.

"I will say that, you know, candidates will answer for their own ads, that, you know, I probably wouldn't run an ad like that, but every candidate gets to make their own decision," he told WSYX-TV, external in the city of Columbus.

Political attack ads are not a new feature of US politics, but David Lublin, a professor from American University's School of Public Affairs, told the BBC that "they have become more intense, and the boundaries have stretched in terms of what one attacks about".
Lublin said it was not new for relatives to be used against a political opponent, mentioning family members who testified against Robert F Kennedy Jr before he was confirmed as health secretary.
"But this is of a different order," he said. "They're estranged not over policy but over a rape allegation."

Lublin believes President Donald Trump's rhetoric and campaigns have helped act as a catalyst for the coarsening of American political discourse - mentioning the time Trump mocked a reporter in Ohio who had a disability.

"We live in an age where certainly many candidates can appear mean and even inappropriate at times," Lublin said, adding: "The key purpose of attack ads isn't necessarily to convert the followers of your opponent, but more to depress their turnout."

He expects the Ramaswamy attack ad to backfire, saying it could be an indication that his campaign is desperate to swing momentum in his favour in the increasingly competitive race for Ohio governor - even though a Democrat has not been elected governor there in over two decades.

Cook Political Report, a nonpartisan website that rates and tracks US elections, has moved the Ohio governor's race from "leans Republican" to "toss up", meaning neither candidate has a clear advantage.

articles.title: Airbnb hosts can no longer make guests strip beds and wash dishes under new rules
articles.summary: The updated policy will apply to all reservations booked on the accommodation site on or after 20 November.

blocks.text: Airbnb has changed its rules to limit what property hosts may ask guests to do - including when it comes to cleaning.
The updated guidelines state that hosts can now set seven standard house rules and can also add other "reasonable" requests.
Airbnb states that guests - who are required to pay a cleaning fee - should not be asked to complete tasks normally done by a cleaner, including washing dishes and stripping beds.
The new rules will apply to all reservations booked on or after 20 November on the accommodation marketplace.
"House rules help guests understand what hosts expect, but we've heard from our community that they can be confusing, onerous and hard to manage," Airbnb told the BBC.
"So, we've redesigned them to make them easier to discover and clearer to set, alongside a new policy that keeps requests reasonable, with no surprises."

According to the new requirements on the Airbnb website, hosts are generally not allowed to ask guests to complete tasks that "require significant effort or time, or would typically be performed by a cleaner, including stripping the bed, taking trash offsite, or washing and putting away dishes".
The company said it may grant exceptions in some circumstances. For example, guests can be asked to limit shower time if there are local drought-related water restrictions.
A property's rules will be displayed to guests more prominently moving forward and will appear in the guests' reservation reminders.
Contracts will only be allowed in limited circumstances, including when required by law or homeowners association rules.
While a host will not be able to impose fines, they remain in control of their house rules and requests, the company said.
If a host's request does not follow Airbnb policies, the issue will be flagged and the owner can appeal if they disagree.
Guests have for years complained about unreasonable tasks they we required to complete before departure, especially as they are required to pay cleaning fees.

TikTok videos from Airbnb hosts Cassie and Jon that show them closely inspecting their rental property in the US state of Georgia after guests leave have gone viral recently for their attention to detail.
One video from the couple, for example, accuses guests of "disrespecting the house rules" for leaving a television remote out of place.
They have been criticised for their strict rules and high standards but said in response that their content had been misinterpreted
Their videos have inspired other content creators to parody stringent hosts.
